facts.statement: The genus Sinocyamodus was described by Li in the year 2000.
The type species of the genus is Sinocyamodus xinpuensis.
Fossils of Sinocyamodus date to the Late Triassic (Tuvalian) stage.
Sinocyamodus is an extinct placodont reptile found in the Xiaowa Formation of China during the Late Triassic.
facts.quote: Sinocyamodus is an extinct genus of placodont reptile from the Late Triassic (Tuvalian) Xiaowa Formation of China.

facts.statement: Sinocyamodus was the first placodont discovered in the eastern Tethys, challenging the previous belief that these reptiles were only found in the western Tethys.
facts.quote: This genus was the first placodont to be discovered in the eastern Tethys, overthrowing traditional views that the group was restricted to the western Tethys.

facts.statement: A 2018 report of an adult Sinocyamodus specimen revealed morphological differences from sub-adults, indicating significant developmental changes with age.
facts.quote: The first adult specimen of this genus was reported in 2018, and showed a number of morphological differences with previously discovered sub-adult material indicating developmental changes with age.

facts.statement: Sinocyamodus belongs to the family Cyamodontidae.
Sinocyamodus is classified within the class Reptilia.
The time range for Sinocyamodus is the Carnian stage, between 233.6 and 227.3 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Carnian to Carnian (233.6 to 227.3 million years ago)
